title: Create a Taylor Series Linearization Survey Design — as_survey
text: data data.frame containing survey responses. Must least one row unique column names. ids <tidy-select> Cluster (PSU) ID column(s). single-stage: ids = psu. multi-stage: ids = c(psu, ssu). Omit entirely simple random sampling. probs <tidy-select> Sampling probability column (single column, values (0, 1]). Converted weights = 1/probs stored internally. used together weights unless values consistent (weights == 1/probs). weights <tidy-select> Sampling weight column (single column, values strictly > 0). strata <tidy-select> Stratification variable column (single column). fpc <tidy-select> Finite population correction column (single column). Accepts either total population size (integer) sampling fraction (numeric, 0–1). contain NA. nest Logical. TRUE, PSU IDs treated nested within strata — .e., ID value two different strata refers two distinct PSUs. Set nest = TRUE PSU IDs globally unique (e.g., NHANES, PSU IDs restart 1 stratum). Requires strata specified. Default FALSE.

text: phase1 survey_taylor object representing Phase 1 design. @data must contain rows phases, plus logical indicator column Phase 2 membership. Create as_survey(). ids2 <tidy-select> Phase 2 cluster ID column(s). single-stage Phase 2: ids2 = psu2. multi-stage: ids2 = c(psu2, ssu2). Omit Phase 2 within-stratum clustering. strata2 <tidy-select> Phase 2 stratification column (single column). Optional. probs2 <tidy-select> Phase 2 inclusion probability column (single column, values (0, 1]). Optional. fpc2 <tidy-select> Phase 2 finite population correction column (single column). Optional. subset <tidy-select> Single logical column phase1@data. TRUE = row selected Phase 2; FALSE = Phase 1 . Required. Must contain TRUE FALSE values (non-degenerate). method Character. title: Create a Two-Phase Survey Design — as_survey_twophase
text: "full" — Full two-phase variance formula. Accounts variability phases. Requires Phase 2 design information (probs2, ids2, strata2) Phase 2 simple random subsample. none provided, warning issued Phase 2 selection treated SRS within Phase 1 strata. "approx" — Approximation ignores Phase 1 sampling variability. Faster less accurate "full" Phase 1 sampling fraction non-negligible. "simple" — Treats Phase 2 single-phase design, ignoring Phase 1. valid Phase 1 census (sampling). Issues warning Phase 1 PSU cluster variables, understates variance clustered designs.

title: Create a Two-Phase Survey Design — as_survey_twophase
code: # Minimal two-phase design: Phase 1 = full cohort, Phase 2 = random subset df <- data.frame(   id        = 1:20,   wt        = rep(2, 20),   in_phase2 = c(rep(TRUE, 10), rep(FALSE, 10)),   y         = rnorm(20) ) phase1 <- as_survey(df, weights = wt) d2 <- as_survey_twophase(phase1, subset = in_phase2) #> Warning: ! No Phase 2 design information provided with `method = "full"`. Phase 2 #>   selection treated as simple random subsampling within Phase 1 strata.  # With Phase 2 stratification and inclusion probabilities df2 <- data.frame(   id          = 1:30,   wt          = rep(3, 30),   in_phase2   = c(rep(TRUE, 15), rep(FALSE, 15)),   arm         = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 10),   subsamprate = rep(c(0.5, 0.7, 0.3), 10),   y           = rnorm(30) ) phase1b <- as_survey(df2, weights = wt) d2b <- as_survey_twophase(   phase1b,   strata2 = arm,   probs2  = subsamprate,   subset  = in_phase2,   method  = "full" )

title: surveycore 0.1.0
text: as_survey() creates survey_taylor objects tidy-select interface (ids, weights, strata, fpc, probs); supports Taylor linearization stratified, clustered, SRS designs. as_survey_rep() creates survey_replicate objects; supports BRR, Fay BRR, JK1, JK2, JKn, bootstrap, ACS, successive-difference replicate schemes. as_survey_twophase() creates survey_twophase objects; supports “full”, “approx”, “simple” two-phase variance estimation methods. update_design() modifies design variables existing survey object without reconstructing scratch; respects validate = TRUE/FALSE. get_means() returns weighted mean standard error via Taylor linearization replicate weights; respects getOption("survey.lonely.psu") single-PSU strata. get_totals() returns weighted total standard error using dispatch get_means(). Metadata setters: set_var_label(), set_variable_labels(), set_val_labels(), set_value_labels(), set_question_preface(), set_question_prefaces(), set_var_note(), set_variable_notes().
